absent: Locking, serialization, and concurrency rules for the emulation context and its operations table are not shown.
Protected mode interrupt vectoring, privilege checks, and error code handling beyond real mode are not shown.
Stack limit validation for real mode interrupt and return paths is noted as future work and not shown.
Complete 32-bit task switch tail and the bodies of the generic task switch entry helpers are absent due to truncation.
Failure modes and side effects of descriptor loaders, linear memory helpers, and control register and model specific register accessors are not shown.
Lifecycle and invalidation rules for the cached input output permission flag across instructions are not shown.
Layout and limits of task state segments and descriptor tables beyond the fields touched here are not shown.

findings.text: A public real mode interrupt entry first marks cached register state invalid, delegates to the internal real mode delivery routine, and only writes registers back when delegation reports successful continuation.

Real mode interrupt delivery saves processor flags, code selector and instruction pointer on the emulated stack in order, clears interrupt trap and alignment controls, then fetches a four byte vector entry from the interrupt table base plus scaled vector number and installs the fetched code selector while transferring control to the fetched offset.

Interrupt and return from interrupt emulation only completes in real mode in these fragments; virtual eighty six and all protected variants including sixteen, thirty two and sixty four bit forms report an unhandleable outcome.

Real mode return from interrupt pops instruction offset, code selector and flags using the current operand width, faults with general protection when the offset exceeds sixteen bits, reloads the code descriptor, merges restored flags through a preserved mask that differs for two versus four byte forms, normalizes reserved and fixed bits, and clears the nonmaskable interrupt mask.

Far jump and far return obtain a two byte selector located beyond the operand, request privileged code descriptor installation tagged with the current privilege level and a transfer kind distinguishing call jump from return, then assign a far instruction pointer; assignment failure is converted to unhandleable rather than propagated.

Near absolute jump only repoints the instruction pointer, near absolute call saves the prior pointer before repointing and then pushes the saved value, near return pops a pointer before repointing, and far return with immediate additionally advances the emulated stack pointer by the immediate operand after completing the far return.

One compare exchange form preserves original memory and accumulator values, performs an internal compare, on equal writes the preserved source into the destination without touching the accumulator and on unequal redirects the result into the accumulator while rewriting the observed destination value to keep a write cycle.

Eight byte compare exchange rejects sixteen byte operands as unhandleable, compares the paired accumulator and data registers against the eight byte memory image, on mismatch loads the memory image into that pair and clears zero flag, on match stores the paired source registers into memory and sets zero flag.
Segment pointer load reads a selector from beyond the operand, installs the descriptor for the segment identified by a second operand, and copies the operand pointer value into the destination.

Resume from system management checks system management membership first and faults as invalid opcode when outside, requests exit from that mode and signals triple fault when exit reports failure, otherwise recalculates the emulation mode and returns that outcome.

The helper builds flat code and stack descriptors with zero base, four kilobyte granularity, four gigabyte limit, present and accessed markings, thirty two bit defaults, supervisor privilege, code marked executable readable and stack marked writable, leaving long and privilege fields for later adjustment.

System call emulation faults as invalid opcode in real and virtual eighty six modes, on Intel compatible guests outside sixty four bit mode, and when system call extensions are disabled; otherwise it derives code and stack selectors from the upper half of the STAR control, installs flat descriptors, saves return address into the counter register, and in long mode saves flags and loads a target plus flag mask from long mode controls while in legacy mode loads a truncated target and clears virtual and interrupt controls before latching single step state from trap flag.

System enter faults with general protection in real mode and when its code control is zero, faults as invalid opcode for non Intel guests in compatibility long mode, reports unhandleable in sixty four bit mode, otherwise clears virtual and interrupt controls, installs code and stack selectors derived from the enter code control, loads instruction and stack pointers from matching controls with truncation outside long mode, and promotes emulation to sixty four bit mode when long mode is active.

System exit faults with general protection in real and virtual eighty six modes, selects thirty two versus sixty four bit user mode from the wide prefix bit, forces user privilege into fresh descriptors, derives selectors from the enter code control with mode specific offsets and zero validation, validates canonical form of counter and data registers in sixty four bit mode, forces requestor privilege bits, then installs segments and loads instruction pointer, mode and stack pointer from data, counter and selected mode.

Permission precheck reports no fault in real mode, always requires permission validation in virtual eighty six mode, and otherwise compares current privilege against the privilege field extracted from flags.
The main backdoor port number equals hexadecimal 5658 and the companion remote port equals hexadecimal 5659.

Input output authorization bypasses checks for the two backdoor ports when the backdoor feature is enabled; otherwise it requires a present task register with sufficient limit, reads a bitmap offset from deep inside the task state, bounds checks the requested port against the limit, reads a two byte permission entry covering the port, and denies when any covered bit is set.
Task state carries its input output permission bitmap pointer at byte offset 102 and requires a minimum scaled limit of 103 for permission validation.
Port permission results are cached in a sticky flag; once set, later checks succeed without revalidation, otherwise a privilege precheck gates whether the detailed bitmap test runs.

For thirty two bit address size on guests whose vendor triple matches Intel, string move and store operations with zeroed counter clear the full counter and truncate source and destination indices to thirty two bits.

Sixteen bit task state save captures instruction offset, flags, eight general registers and five selectors including local descriptor table, while load restores offset and flags with bit one forced plus registers, installs selectors before descriptors, derives privilege from incoming code selector, and loads local table plus four segment descriptors under task switch semantics where later faults belong to the new task.

Thirty two bit save captures instruction pointer, flags, general registers and six selectors while intentionally omitting page table base and local table selector; load installs page table base with general protection failure, restores pointer and flags with bit one forced plus registers, installs selectors before descriptors, selects virtual eighty six versus protected thirty two bit mode from the virtual flag, derives privilege accordingly, and loads local table plus six segment descriptors under task switch semantics.

Both task switch widths read and persist the outgoing image, fetch the incoming image via the new descriptor base, and unless the outgoing selector equals all ones write it as the previous link into the incoming image before loading the incoming state; the thirty two bit form persists only the range from instruction pointer through selectors.

Several paths lack complete handling: protected interrupt and return paths, sixty four bit enter path and sixteen byte compare exchange report unhandleable; far jump and return note missing error handling; real return notes missing stack limit validation; failed system management exit escalates to triple fault; noncanonical exit pointers fault.
This lane depends on an external copy helper owned elsewhere.
